questions.q: What does the equation Av = λv mean geometrically?
options: v is a row of the matrix A
v is rotated by 90 degrees when multiplied by A
A has no effect on v at all
v is scaled by λ but its direction is unchanged when multiplied by A
questions.explain: An eigenvector v keeps its direction (up to sign if λ is negative) after being multiplied by A; it is only scaled by the eigenvalue λ.

questions.q: For A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], what are the eigenvalues, found from det(A - λI) = 0?
options: λ = -1 and λ = -3
λ = 1 and λ = 3
λ = 2 and λ = 2
λ = 0 and λ = 4
questions.explain: det(A - λI) = (2-λ)^2 - 1 = λ^2 - 4λ + 3 = (λ-1)(λ-3), so the eigenvalues are 1 and 3.

questions.q: Why does a real symmetric matrix (like a covariance matrix) always have real eigenvalues?
options: Because all its entries are positive
Because symmetric matrices are always diagonal already
Because it always has determinant 1
This is a guaranteed property of real symmetric matrices, unlike general square matrices which can have complex eigenvalues
questions.explain: A theorem of linear algebra guarantees that real symmetric matrices have only real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors, unlike general matrices which can have complex eigenvalues.

questions.q: In the spectral decomposition A = QΛQ^T of a symmetric matrix, what do the columns of Q and the diagonal of Λ represent?
options: Q is always the identity matrix
Q holds row sums and Λ holds column sums
Q's columns are the orthogonal eigenvectors and Λ's diagonal holds the corresponding eigenvalues
Λ holds the original matrix entries unchanged
questions.explain: The spectral decomposition expresses A in terms of its orthogonal eigenvectors (columns of Q) and its eigenvalues (diagonal entries of Λ).

questions.q: For a discrete-time system x_(t+1) = A*x_t, under what condition is the system stable (converges to zero rather than exploding)?
options: When every eigenvalue of A has magnitude less than 1
When A is symmetric
When A is the identity matrix
When A has a zero determinant
questions.explain: The system's long-run behavior is governed by powers of A, which shrink to zero exactly when every eigenvalue has magnitude strictly less than 1.
